question: Which of the following is the fastest way to open the Help window in Microsoft Word?
option_1: Type ‘help’ in the search bar and then, press Enter
option_2: Click the Microsoft Office button and then, click Help
option_4: Click the Help button on the ribbon
solution_text:
The correct answer is Press F1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pressing the F1 key is the fastest, universal keyboard shortcut to open the Help window/pane in Microsoft Word (and across most MS Office applications). (सहायता विंडो — F1 कुंजी)

 

• The F1 function key is a standard convention across virtually all Microsoft Office programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) for instantly launching context-sensitive Help, without needing the mouse.

 

• This single keystroke bypasses the need to navigate menus, ribbons, or search bars, making it the quickest route to Help.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In older Office versions (pre-2007 ribbon interface), the Microsoft Office button (or File menu) also contained a Help option, but this requires more clicks than F1.

 

• Similarly, F1 opens Help in Windows itself and in many other software applications, reflecting its long-standing status as the default Help shortcut.

 

NOTE

 

• Type 'help' in the search bar and then, press Enter (Option 1): This works in newer versions with a Tell Me/search bar, but requires typing first, making it slower than a single keypress.

 

• Click the Microsoft Office button and then, click Help (Option 2): This is a multi-step mouse action and is slower than the F1 shortcut; it is also specific to the older Office button interface.

 

• Click the Help button on the ribbon (Option 4): This also requires locating and clicking a ribbon icon with the mouse, which takes longer than pressing F1.

question: Which star is also known as the ‘Pole Star’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The North star.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pole Star, also called Polaris or Dhruva Tara, is popularly known as the North Star because it lies almost directly above the Earth's North Pole, very close to the north celestial pole. (ध्रुव तारा — उत्तर तारा)

 

• It appears nearly stationary in the sky while other stars appear to rotate around it, because it lies almost on the Earth's rotational axis extended into space.

 

• Polaris belongs to the constellation Ursa Minor (Little Bear) and has historically been used by sailors and travellers for navigation in the Northern Hemisphere, since its altitude above the horizon roughly equals the observer's latitude.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In Hindu mythology, the Pole Star is associated with the legend of Dhruva, a devotee of Lord Vishnu who was granted a permanent place in the sky.

 

• There is no fixed 'South Star' as prominent as Polaris; navigators in the Southern Hemisphere instead use the Southern Cross (Crux) constellation to locate the south celestial pole.

 

NOTE

 

• The West star (Option 1): There is no star designated as a fixed 'West star'; west is a cardinal direction, not marked by any single fixed star.

 

• The South star (Option 2): No single bright star marks the south celestial pole the way Polaris marks the north; the Southern Cross is used instead.

 

• The East star (Option 4): Similarly, there is no fixed 'East star' used for orientation.

question: According to Census 2011, which union territory recorded the highest female literacy rate in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshadweep.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Lakshadweep recorded the highest female literacy rate among all Union Territories, at approximately 88%. (जनगणना 2011 — लक्षद्वीप)

 

• Lakshadweep also recorded the second-highest overall literacy rate (91.85%) among all States/UTs in India, just behind Kerala.

 

• The high literacy of Lakshadweep — a small union territory in the Arabian Sea comprising 36 islands — is attributed to its small, close-knit population and focused welfare and education initiatives.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala has the highest overall literacy rate among Indian states (94.0%, Census 2011), and also leads in female literacy among states.

 

• Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate among states in Census 2011.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi (Option 1): Delhi's female literacy rate (around 80.93%) was lower than that of Lakshadweep.

 

• Chandigarh (Option 3): Chandigarh's female literacy rate (around 76.65%) was also lower.

 

• Puducherry (Option 4): Puducherry's female literacy rate (around 81.22%) was likewise lower than Lakshadweep's.

question: In Equestrian sports, ______ occurs when a horse or rider lowers an element of a jump that establishes the height of an obstacle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is knockdown.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In show jumping (equestrian sport), a knockdown occurs when the horse or rider dislodges or lowers the top rail (or another height-defining element) of a jump/obstacle, and it falls to the ground. (नॉकडाउन — बाधा गिरना)

 

• A knockdown results in penalty points (faults) being added to the competitor's score, typically 4 faults in modern show jumping rules.

 

• The term is specific to jumping obstacles and is distinct from a refusal (where the horse stops before the jump) or a fall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Equestrian events at the Olympics include Dressage, Show Jumping, and Eventing.

 

• A 'clean round' (a distractor option here) refers to completing the course with no faults at all — the opposite scenario of a knockdown.

 

NOTE

 

• canter (Option 1): A canter is a controlled, three-beat gait of the horse, faster than a trot but slower than a gallop — unrelated to knocking down a jump element.

 

• curb (Option 2): A curb refers to a type of bit or strap used to control the horse, not to an obstacle-related fault.

 

• clean round (Option 3): A clean round means the horse completes the course without any faults, which is the opposite of a knockdown.

question: Which group of states was concentrated in the cotton production in the early years to develop textile industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra and Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the early years of India's industrialisation, the cotton textile industry was concentrated mainly in Maharashtra (Bombay) and Gujarat (Ahmedabad). (सूती वस्त्र उद्योग — महाराष्ट्र और गुजरात)

 

• These regions were favoured because of their proximity to cotton-growing black soil (regur) tracts of the Deccan Plateau, a humid climate suited to spinning, access to the port of Bombay for imports/exports, and easy availability of capital and labour.

 

• Bombay came to be called the 'Cottonopolis of India', and Ahmedabad became known as the 'Manchester of India' due to their dominance in cotton textile manufacturing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first cotton textile mill in India was set up in Bombay in 1854 by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar.

 

• Coimbatore and Madurai in Tamil Nadu later also emerged as important cotton textile centres in South India.

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal and Odisha (Option 1): These regions were historically known for jute production and the jute textile industry (centred around Kolkata/Hooghly), not cotton.

 

• Bihar and West Bengal (Option 2): These states were not the early centres of the cotton textile industry.

 

• Punjab and Haryana (Option 4): While cotton is grown here, these states became prominent cotton-growing areas later (post-Green Revolution) and were not the early centres of the textile industry.

question: Which of the following hills is located in the Eastern most part of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Patkai Bum Hills.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Patkai Bum Hills (also called the Patkai Range) are located in the easternmost part of India, forming a natural boundary between India (Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland) and Myanmar. (पटकाई बम पहाड़ियाँ — पूर्वी सीमा)

 

• The Patkai hills are part of the Purvanchal (Eastern Hills) ranges and run along the India–Myanmar border, branching further south into the Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, and Mizo (Lushai) Hills.

 

• They are composed of strong sandstones and are covered with thick, tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Purvanchal Hills as a whole include the Patkai Bum, Naga, Manipur, Mizo, and Tripura hills, and separate India from Myanmar.

 

• The Stilwell Road, an important historical road built during World War II, passes through the Patkai Hills connecting Assam to Myanmar and China.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaintia Hills (Option 2): Located in Meghalaya, part of the Meghalaya Plateau, not the easternmost region.

 

• Khasi Hills (Option 3): Also located in Meghalaya, forming part of the Meghalaya Plateau.

 

• Garo Hills (Option 4): Located in the western part of Meghalaya, making them the westernmost of the Meghalaya hill ranges, not the easternmost part of India.

question: Who among the following is NOT associated with the Green Revolution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is P Chidambaram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• P Chidambaram is an Indian politician best known as a former Union Finance Minister and Home Minister; he has no association with India's Green Revolution of the 1960s. (हरित क्रांति — पी चिदंबरम असंबंधित)

 

• The Green Revolution in India (mid-1960s) was driven by agricultural scientist Dr. M. S. Swaminathan (the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'), agronomist Norman Borlaug (the global 'Father of the Green Revolution', who developed high-yielding wheat varieties), and Union Agriculture Minister C. Subramaniam (Chidambaram Subramaniam), who implemented the policy at the government level.

 

• The Green Revolution significantly boosted foodgrain (especially wheat and rice) production in India through high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, irrigation, and fertilizers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Norman Borlaug won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his contribution to the Green Revolution globally.

 

• M. S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously (announced 2024) in recognition of his contribution to Indian agriculture.

 

NOTE

 

• MS Swaminathan (Option 1): Widely regarded as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India', closely associated with the movement.

 

• Norman Borlaug (Option 3): Known globally as the 'Father of the Green Revolution', developed the high-yielding wheat varieties central to it.

 

• Chidambaram Subramaniam (Option 4): As Union Minister of Agriculture (1964-1967), he played the key administrative role in implementing the Green Revolution in India.

question: Who among the following is related to Hindustani classical singing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mallikarjun Mansur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mallikarjun Mansur was a renowned exponent of Hindustani classical vocal music, belonging to the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana. (हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय गायन — मल्लिकार्जुन मंसूर)

 

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (1992) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Hindustani classical music, and was known for his khayal singing.

 

• He hailed from Karnataka, showing that Hindustani classical music (the North Indian classical tradition) is practised and mastered by artists across India, not only in the north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The two major classical music traditions of India are Hindustani classical music (North Indian) and Carnatic classical music (South Indian).

 

• Other notable Jaipur-Atrauli gharana vocalists include Kesarbai Kerkar and Kishori Amonkar.

 

NOTE

 

• Srinavasa Iyer (Option 2): Associated with Carnatic classical music, the South Indian tradition.

 

• Aruna Sairam (Option 3): A well-known Carnatic vocalist, not a Hindustani singer.

 

• Ramanuj Iyengar (Option 4): Associated with the Carnatic music tradition, not Hindustani classical singing.

question: The original constitution did NOT mention any fundamental duty because:
option_1: initially fundamental duties were not expected to be performed
option_2: it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly
option_3: it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties forcefully
option_4: initially fundamental duties were punishable as per the constitution
solution_text:
The correct answer is it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The original Constitution of India (1950) did not contain a chapter on Fundamental Duties, as the framers believed citizens would perform their civic duties voluntarily and out of a sense of responsibility, without needing an explicit constitutional mandate. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — स्वेच्छा से पालन)

 

• Fundamental Duties were added later, through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, inserting Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution.

 

• Originally 10 duties were added; an 11th duty (regarding the duty of parents/guardians to provide education to children) was added later by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be directly enforced through courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Initially fundamental duties were not expected to be performed (Option 1): Incorrect; the framers still expected citizens to fulfil civic duties, only not as constitutionally listed obligations.

 

• It was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties forcefully (Option 3): Incorrect; there was no expectation of force involved, only voluntary compliance.

 

• Initially fundamental duties were punishable as per the constitution (Option 4): Incorrect and factually wrong; Fundamental Duties, even after being added in 1976, carry no direct legal punishment for non-compliance.

question: Which of the following measures can be adopted by the government to reduce revenue deficit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tax reforms.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Revenue deficit occurs when the government's revenue expenditure exceeds its revenue receipts. It can be reduced either by increasing revenue receipts or by cutting revenue expenditure. (राजस्व घाटा — कर सुधार)

 

• Tax reforms — such as broadening the tax base, improving tax compliance, and rationalising tax rates — help increase revenue receipts (tax revenue) for the government, thereby directly reducing the revenue deficit.

 

• Other standard measures to reduce revenue deficit include cutting unproductive/non-essential revenue expenditure, and improving the efficiency of public sector enterprises to boost non-tax revenue (dividends, disinvestment proceeds, etc.).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts excluding borrowings; it is a broader measure than revenue deficit.

 

• The FRBM Act, 2003 (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act) was enacted to institutionalise fiscal discipline and reduce deficits.

 

NOTE

 

• Offering freebies (Option 1): This is a form of revenue expenditure and would increase, not reduce, the revenue deficit.

 

• Increasing subsidies (Option 2): Subsidies are also revenue expenditure; increasing them would widen, not reduce, the revenue deficit.

 

• Increasing money supply (Option 3): This is a monetary policy tool (used to manage inflation/liquidity) and does not directly address the government's revenue-expenditure gap.

question: Every year in the month of February, this camel festival is organised by Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation in __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bikaner.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Camel Festival is organised annually by the Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation (RTDC) in Bikaner, Rajasthan. (ऊंट महोत्सव — बीकानेर)

 

• The festival celebrates the camel — the 'Ship of the Desert' — through camel decoration/beauty contests, camel races, camel dances, and folk music and dance performances, held at the Bikaner Junagarh Fort grounds.

 

• Bikaner is famous for its camel-breeding farm (the National Research Centre on Camel) and is often called the desert region most associated with camels in Rajasthan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan hosts several RTDC-organised festivals, including the Desert Festival in Jaisalmer and the Marwar Festival in Jodhpur.

 

• The Pushkar Camel Fair (in Ajmer district) is a separate, larger livestock fair held around Kartik Purnima (October-November).

 

NOTE

 

• Barmer (Option 1): Known for the Thar Festival, not the RTDC Camel Festival.

 

• Jaisalmer (Option 3): Known for the Desert Festival, a separate RTDC event.

 

• Jodhpur (Option 4): Known for the Marwar Festival, a different RTDC event, not the Camel Festival.

question: MLAs in which of the following states/UTs received an increase of about 66% in salaries and allowances w.e.f. 14 February 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Delhi Legislative Assembly passed a bill increasing the salaries and allowances of MLAs by about 66%, effective 14 February 2023. (दिल्ली विधायक वेतन वृद्धि — 66%)

 

• With this hike, the total monthly salary/allowances of a Delhi MLA increased from around ₹54,000 to about ₹90,000; this was the first such increase since 2011.

 

• The bill required the assent of the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, since Delhi is a Union Territory with a legislature, and this assent was granted before the hike took effect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Delhi's MLA salary, even after this hike, remained among the lowest in India compared to other states.

 

• Salaries and allowances of legislators are decided by respective State Legislatures/UT Assemblies and can vary widely across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Did not implement a comparable 66% MLA salary hike effective 14 February 2023.

 

• Lakshadweep (Option 2): As a Union Territory without a legislative assembly of its own during this period, this is not applicable.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Did not implement this specific salary revision on this date.

question: From which book is the national song of India compiled?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anand Math.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's National Song, 'Vande Mataram', was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in Sanskrit/Bengali and is taken from his novel Anandmath (Anand Math), published in 1882. (राष्ट्रगीत वंदे मातरम् — आनंद मठ)

 

• 'Vande Mataram' was first sung publicly at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress and was formally adopted as the National Song by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950, the same day the National Anthem was adopted.

 

• 'Vande Mataram' has equal status with the National Anthem ('Jana Gana Mana'), though the two are distinct — the anthem was written by Rabindranath Tagore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anandmath is set against the backdrop of the Sannyasi Rebellion in Bengal and reflects nationalist sentiment against British rule.

 

• 'Jana Gana Mana', the National Anthem, is taken from Tagore's Brahmo hymn 'Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata'.

 

NOTE

 

• Mandukya Upanishad (Option 2): One of the ancient Upanishads, source of 'Satyameva Jayate' (India's national motto), not the national song.

 

• Katha Upanishad (Option 3): Another ancient Upanishad text, unrelated to the National Song.

 

• Bharat Bharti (Option 4): A patriotic work by Hindi poet Maithili Sharan Gupt, not the source of the National Song.

question:
With reference to ‘Saila dance’ consider the following statements and select the correct option.

a) A group comprising of male performers.

b) The dance is performed with bamboo sticks.

c) It is performed after the cutting of crops.
solution_text:
The correct answer is a, b, c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saila (Shaila) dance is a popular folk dance of Chhattisgarh, performed mainly by the Gond tribal community. All three statements about it are correct. (सैला नृत्य — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• Statement (a) is correct: Saila is essentially a male dance, performed by a group of male performers/dancers.

 

• Statement (b) is correct: The dancers hold and rhythmically strike bamboo sticks against each other while dancing to the beat of drums (mandar/dhol), similar in style to stick dances like Dandiya.

 

• Statement (c) is correct: It is a post-harvest dance, traditionally performed after the cutting/harvesting of crops, as part of harvest celebrations in Chhattisgarhi villages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important folk dances of Chhattisgarh include Panthi (performed by the Satnami community), Raut Nacha (by the Yadav/cowherd community), and Karma dance.

 

• Saila dance is often performed during festivals and is accompanied by folk songs praising nature, harvest and community life.

 

NOTE

 

• Both b and c (Option 2): Incomplete, as it wrongly excludes statement (a), which is also correct.

 

• Both a and c (Option 3): Incomplete, as it wrongly excludes statement (b), which is also correct.

 

• Both a and b (Option 4): Incomplete, as it wrongly excludes statement (c), which is also correct.

question: Who was the first person to conduct a systematic study of chromosomes during division and called this process mitosis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Walther Flemming.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Walther Flemming, a German biologist, conducted the first systematic study of chromosome behaviour during cell division and coined the term 'mitosis' in 1882. (माइटोसिस — वाल्थर फ्लेमिंग)

 

• He discovered chromatin (the thread-like structures inside the nucleus that condense into chromosomes) and described in detail how these structures split and separate during cell division, laying the foundation of cytogenetics.

 

• His work, published in the book *Zellsubstanz, Kern und Zelltheilung* (1882), is considered a landmark in understanding cell biology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Walther Flemming is often regarded, along with Eduard Strasburger and Edouard van Beneden, as one of the founders of the study of chromosome behaviour (cytogenetics).

 

• The term 'chromosome' itself was coined later, in 1888, by Heinrich Wilhelm Waldeyer.

 

NOTE

 

• Friedrich Miescher (Option 1): Discovered nuclein (DNA) in 1869, not associated with naming mitosis.

 

• Thomas Hunt Morgan (Option 2): Known for his work on the chromosome theory of heredity and genetics using fruit flies (Drosophila), for which he won the Nobel Prize in 1933, but he did not coin the term mitosis.

 

• Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (Option 3): Known as the 'Father of Microbiology' for his pioneering work with microscopes and discovery of microorganisms, not for the study of mitosis.

question: In cricket, a fast, head-high delivery of the ball is referred to as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is bouncer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A bouncer in cricket is a short-pitched, fast delivery bowled by the bowler that rises sharply and reaches the batsman around head height, intended to intimidate or surprise the batsman. (बाउंसर — तेज उछाल वाली गेंद)

 

• It is a common short-pitched fast-bowling tactic, bowled by pitching the ball much shorter (closer to the bowler) than a typical delivery, causing it to bounce up steeply.

 

• Excessive use of bouncers is regulated by cricket's playing conditions/laws (e.g., a limit on bouncers per over) to ensure player safety.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A 'yorker' is a delivery pitched right at the batsman's feet/base of the stumps, the opposite in style to a bouncer.

 

• Fast bowlers famous for their bouncers include Dennis Lillee, Malcolm Marshall, and Jasprit Bumrah.

 

NOTE

 

• grubber (Option 1): A grubber is a delivery that stays very low, skidding along the ground instead of bouncing up.

 

• leg-bye (Option 2): A leg-bye is a type of extra run scored when the ball deflects off the batsman's body (not the bat) and the batsmen run; unrelated to delivery type.

 

• duck (Option 3): In cricket, a 'duck' refers to a batsman being dismissed without scoring any runs, not a type of delivery.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the largest Buddhist population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Maharashtra has the largest Buddhist population in India, accounting for around 77% of India's total Buddhist population. (बौद्ध जनसंख्या — महाराष्ट्र)

 

• This is largely due to the mass conversion movement led by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, who converted to Buddhism along with hundreds of thousands of his followers (mainly from the Mahar community) at Nagpur (Deekshabhoomi) in 1956, giving rise to the Navayana (Neo-Buddhist) movement.

 

• Buddhism, though it originated in India, constitutes a relatively small percentage of India's overall population, but has significant regional concentration in Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other states with notable Buddhist populations include Uttar Pradesh (linked to important Buddhist sites like Sarnath and Kushinagar) and the north-eastern/Himalayan states of Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh, and Tripura, where Buddhism has traditional/tribal roots.

 

• Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur is regarded as one of the most sacred sites for Neo-Buddhists in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Has an important historical Buddhist heritage (Sarnath, Kushinagar) but a much smaller Buddhist population share than Maharashtra.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Has notable Buddhist sites like Sanchi, but a comparatively small Buddhist population.

 

• West Bengal (Option 4): Also has a smaller Buddhist population compared to Maharashtra.

question: Who captained India to victory in the 2011 Cricket World Cup final win over Sri Lanka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahendra Singh Dhoni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahendra Singh Dhoni captained the Indian cricket team to victory in the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup, defeating Sri Lanka in the final held at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, on 2 April 2011. (2011 विश्व कप विजेता कप्तान — महेंद्र सिंह धोनी)

 

• Dhoni famously finished the match with a six, and was named Man of the Match in the final for his unbeaten innings of 91 runs.

 

• This win made India the first team to win the Cricket World Cup final on home soil, and the second team (after West Indies) to win the World Cup as co-hosts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 World Cup was jointly hosted by India, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh.

 

• India had earlier won the ODI World Cup in 1983, under the captaincy of Kapil Dev.

 

NOTE

 

• Sourav Ganguly (Option 1): Captained India to the 2003 World Cup final, where India lost to Australia.

 

• Sachin Tendulkar (Option 3): A key player in the 2011 winning squad and 'Player of the Tournament', but he was not the captain.

 

• Rahul Dravid (Option 4): A former India captain in other formats/periods, but not part of the 2011 World Cup-winning squad's leadership.

question: Which function is used to calculate the maximum value in a selected column in MS Excel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Max.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Excel, the MAX() function is used to find the highest (maximum) value within a selected range of cells, such as a column. (अधिकतम मान फलन — MAX)

 

• The general syntax is =MAX(number1, [number2], ...) or =MAX(range), e.g. `=MAX(A1:A10)` returns the largest value among cells A1 to A10.

 

• Excel also provides the complementary MIN() function to find the smallest value in a range.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common statistical functions in Excel include AVERAGE() (mean), COUNT() (counts numeric entries), and SUM() (adds values).

 

• Excel functions are entered by typing '=' followed by the function name and arguments in parentheses.

 

NOTE

 

• Auto max (Option 1): Not a valid or existing Excel function name.

 

• High (Option 2): Not a valid Excel function name.

 

• Auto high (Option 4): Not a valid Excel function name.

question: Which British colonel is remembered as the Butcher of Amritsar for his role in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reginald Dyer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Brigadier-General Reginald Edward Harry Dyer ordered his troops to open fire on an unarmed, peaceful crowd gathered at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, on 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day), killing hundreds of people. (जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड — रेजिनाल्ड डायर)

 

• For this brutal act, he became infamously known as the 'Butcher of Amritsar'.

 

• The massacre was a turning point in India's freedom struggle and led Rabindranath Tagore to renounce his knighthood in protest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer (the then Lieutenant Governor of Punjab, who had approved Dyer's actions) in London in 1940, in revenge for the massacre.

 

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre is also known as the Amritsar massacre.

 

NOTE

 

• Robert Clive (Option 2): A British East India Company official associated with the Battle of Plassey (1757), not the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

 

• William Birdwood (Option 3): A British general known for commanding the ANZAC forces at Gallipoli during World War I, unrelated to Jallianwala Bagh.

 

• William Slim (Option 4): A British Field Marshal known for commanding the Fourteenth Army during World War II in Burma, unrelated to this event.

question: Thee 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of Indian Constitution was passed in the year ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1976.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, was passed by the Indian Parliament in 1976, during the Emergency period, under the government of Indira Gandhi. (42वां संविधान संशोधन — 1976)

 

• It is often called the 'Mini Constitution' because of the sweeping changes it made, including the addition of the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble, and the insertion of Fundamental Duties (Article 51A).

 

• The Act came into force in stages, with most provisions effective from 3 January 1977, but it is designated and referred to as the Act of 1976, the year it was enacted/passed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment was based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• Many of the changes made by the 42nd Amendment (like curtailing judicial review) were later modified by the 43rd and 44th Amendment Acts.

 

NOTE

 

• 1977 (Option 2): This is when most provisions of the Act came into effect, but the Act itself is dated/passed in 1976.

 

• 1978 (Option 3): Incorrect; not the year of passage of the 42nd Amendment.

 

• 1979 (Option 4): Incorrect; not the year of passage of the 42nd Amendment.

question: In which of the following liquids would anthracene dissolve easily?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Benzene.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Anthracene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), a non-polar organic solid made of three fused benzene rings. (एन्थ्रासीन — बेंजीन में घुलनशील)

 

• By the principle 'like dissolves like', non-polar substances dissolve readily in non-polar solvents. Benzene, being a non-polar aromatic hydrocarbon solvent, readily dissolves anthracene.

 

• Anthracene is essentially insoluble or only very slightly soluble in polar solvents like water, since polar and non-polar substances do not mix well.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anthracene is used in the production of the red dye alizarin and other dyes, and in organic semiconductors.

 

• Other common non-polar organic solvents include toluene, chloroform, and carbon tetrachloride, which can also dissolve anthracene.

 

NOTE

 

• Sodium chloride (Option 2): This is a solid ionic compound, not a liquid solvent, and would not dissolve a non-polar organic compound like anthracene.

 

• Methane (Option 3): Methane is a gas at room temperature, not a liquid solvent under normal conditions.

 

• Water (Option 4): Water is a highly polar solvent and does not effectively dissolve non-polar compounds like anthracene.

question: In March 2023, the Uttarakhand government had approved how much horizontal reservation for statehood activists in state government jobs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In March 2023, the Uttarakhand government, led by Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, approved 10% horizontal reservation for statehood movement activists/agitators in state government jobs. (उत्तराखंड राज्य आंदोलनकारी आरक्षण — 10%)

 

• This reservation is meant to honour those who participated in the Uttarakhand statehood movement, which led to the creation of Uttarakhand as a separate state on 9 November 2000, carved out of Uttar Pradesh.

 

• The policy was subsequently tabled/approved in the state assembly to formalise this quota within the reservation framework for government recruitment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uttarakhand was created as India's 27th state, along with Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, all formed in the year 2000.

 

• Being a horizontal reservation, this 10% quota for statehood activists cuts across all existing vertical categories (General, OBC, SC, ST) rather than being a separate additional category outside them.

 

NOTE

 

• 15% (Option 2): Incorrect; not the percentage approved for statehood activists' reservation.

 

• 8% (Option 3): Incorrect; not the percentage approved.

 

• 5% (Option 4): Incorrect; not the percentage approved.

question: The Press and Registration of Books (PRB) Act was enacted in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1867.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Press and Registration of Books (PRB) Act was enacted in 1867 by the British colonial government in India. (प्रेस और पुस्तक पंजीकरण अधिनियम — 1867)

 

• The Act mandated the registration of printing presses and newspapers/books, requiring details like the name of the printer, publisher, and place of publication to be declared and printed on every book/newspaper.

 

• It remained the primary law governing the registration of the press and books in India for over 150 years, until it was replaced by the Press and Registration of Periodicals (PRP) Act, 2023.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The PRB Act, 1867, is distinct from other press control laws of the colonial period like the Vernacular Press Act, 1878, which specifically targeted vernacular (Indian language) newspapers.

 

• The Registrar of Newspapers for India (RNI), set up in 1956, administers press registration matters, now under the successor 2023 Act.

 

NOTE

 

• 1887 (Option 1): Incorrect; not the year of enactment of the PRB Act.

 

• 1877 (Option 2): Incorrect; not the year of enactment.

 

• 1857 (Option 4): This is the year of the Revolt of 1857 (First War of Independence), not the year of the PRB Act.

question: Who amongst the following Delhi Sultanate rulers sent his army under Malik Kafur’s command to conquer South India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alauddin Khilji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alauddin Khilji, ruler of the Khilji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, sent his trusted general and slave-commander Malik Kafur on several military campaigns into South India in the early 14th century. (अलाउद्दीन खिलजी — मलिक काफूर दक्षिण भारत अभियान)

 

• Malik Kafur led successful campaigns against the Yadavas of Devagiri, the Kakatiyas of Warangal, the Hoysalas of Dwarasamudra, and the Pandyas of Madurai, extending Delhi Sultanate influence deep into peninsular India and bringing back immense wealth.

 

• Alauddin Khilji's reign (1296-1316 CE) is also noted for market reforms and successfully repelling repeated Mongol invasions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Malik Kafur was later given the title 'Malik Naib' (deputy/regent) by Alauddin Khilji.

 

• After Alauddin Khilji's death, Malik Kafur briefly seized power before being assassinated.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghiyas-ud-din Balban (Option 1): A ruler of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty, known for his 'theory of kingship' and blood-and-iron policy, not associated with sending Malik Kafur south.

 

• Iltutmish (Option 2): Founder-consolidator of the Slave dynasty, known for introducing the silver tanka and copper jital, ruled well before Alauddin Khilji's southern campaigns.

 

• Qutub-al-din Aibak (Option 4): Founder of the Delhi Sultanate (Slave/Mamluk dynasty), began construction of the Qutub Minar; not connected to Malik Kafur's campaigns.
